# iliad-154 (24.200–301) — review, pass 1

Method: notes checked label by label against the form and line; Greek to `l` word by word; `l` to `i`; remembered English; quotation marks; cross-references checked against the source archive (24.149 herald, 24.169–187 Iris, 24.269 ὀμφαλόεν, 24.198–199 closing the last part, iliad-153's last unit closes Priam’s speech with ”); every stock epithet and verb grepped in the two house tables. `t` untouched (verified by script; the units join to the packet lines). No scansion flags in the packet, so no hand scansion was required; the part has no bracketed or skipped lines. `gloss.json` not touched (second pass later). new-renderings.md was updated to match the changes below.

## Changes (line · field · severity · wrong · done)

1. 253 · l (and i, n) · high · the closing ” stood at the end of unit 253–254 in `l`, but Priam’s speech runs on to 264 (and `i` had no ”): the speech was closed four units early · removed the ” from `l`; the speech now closes once, at 263–264, in both layers.
2. 208 · n · medium · κλαίωμεν called an aorist subjunctive; it is the present subjunctive of κλαίω (the aorist stem is κλαυ-) · corrected.
3. 237 · n/l/i · medium · ἐνίσσων rendered "chiding"; ἐνίσσω is a by-form of ἐνίπτω, which the Odyssey table fixes as "rebuke" ("chide" is turned down for ἐνίπτω at 3.438) · "rebuking" in `l` and `i`, note says it is a by-form of ἐνίπτω.
4. 241 · l, i, n · medium · ὀνόσασθ’ rendered "find fault" / "scorn it"; table turns "find fault with" down for ὄνομαι by name (Iliad 4.539) and fixes "make light of" (Odyssey 17.378) · "make light of it" in both layers.
5. 253 · l, i, n · medium · κατηφόνες rendered "disgraces", the word kept for ἐλέγχεα (260) and turned down for κατηφείη (16.498, "a shame") · "shames" in both layers; note adjusted.
6. 279 · i (and l, n) · medium · ὕπαγον ζυγόν "brought … to the yoke" is listed as avoided at 16.148; ἀτίταλλεν "fostered" against the table's "reared" (5.271) · "led horses under the yoke"; "reared" in `l`, `i` and note.
7. 239 · l, i, n · medium · κηδήσοντες "trouble" (table calls "troubled" the weaker word and fixes κήδω "distress", 5.400, 9.615) · "to distress me".
8. 220, 252, 296 · l/i · medium · κελεύω rendered "bidden"/"bade"/"bid" in `l` (and `i` 297 "bid"); the table fixes κελεύω "order" and reserves "bid" for ἄνωγα · "had ordered", "ordered", "would not order you" (`i` "urge you or order you to go").
9. 224–226 · l, i, n · medium · βούλομαι "I am willing"; table fixes "want" (13.347), "wish" being ἐθέλω · "I want it", note explains it is acceptance of such a death.
10. 290–291 · l · medium · ὁρᾶται: `l` "looks down" vs `i` "looks over" disagreed; and the grammar was not hedged (middle or passive form) · `l` "looks about", `i` unchanged; note now says it is a middle/passive form, taken as active "surveys", the passive "is seen" fitting less well.
11. 211–213 · l, i · medium · ἔχοιμι + infinitive: `l` "may I have to eat" reads as obligation in English; `i` dropped "have" altogether · both layers "may I be able to eat/fasten and eat"; the note already said "may I be able to".
12. 226 · n · medium · hard passage γόου ἐξ ἔρον εἵην stated as a flat idiom · note now says it is hard and read as split compound ἐξ … εἵην of ἐξίημι with ἔρον as object.
13. 297–298 · l · low · μάλα περ "very … though" lost in `l` · "very eager though you are". Note on Ἀργείων "third name … in these lines" corrected (it is the third of the names to appear in the part, after Achaeans 203 and Danaans 295).
14. 209 · l · low · τῷ δ’ ὥς: δέ unrendered in `l` · "And for him thus"; note says the δέ gives the reason.
15. 217 · i · low · αὖτε dropped; the 6.440 pattern keeps "in turn" in `i` · "spoke to her in turn".
16. 203 · n · low · "ἐλθέμεν’" with apostrophe, but the line prints ἐλθέμεν (no elision) · corrected to the short epic infinitive form.
17. 270 · n · medium · ὀμφαλόν called a knob "on the pole", but 24.269 calls the yoke ὀμφαλόεν "bossed" · now "a knob on the yoke".
18. 271 · n · low · τὸ μέν asserted to be the yoke; the neuter ζυγόδεσμον just before is the other candidate · hedged.
19. 233 · n · low · τρίποδες described as stands for cauldrons (they may be vessels) · "bronze stands or vessels".
20. 228 · n · low · ἀνέῳγεν has pluperfect shape · stated.
21. 223 · n · low · ἐσδέρκομαι lemma given with its usual εἰσδέρκομαι form.
22. 242 · i · low · μᾶλλον "much easier" overstated · "all the easier".
23. 248 · i · low · τε-chain dropped "and" before Pammon and Deiphobus · restored.
24. 257, 261, 268, 300 · n · low · ἔσκε "old form" → iterative; χοροιτυπίῃσιν "dative" → dative plural; "colon" → "raised stop" at 268 (`l` has a semicolon); οὐ μέν τοι "certainly not" misleads (denial of disobeying) → "surely not".

## Considered and refused

- 24.222 (= 2.81): kept word for word as published; the "past condition" label in the note is acceptable for imperfect ἐκέλευεν + κεν with optative.
- 24.211 ἀργίποδας "quick-footed": kept, with the note's "possibly white-footed"; consistent with the table's κύνες ἀργοί "swift dogs".
- 24.247 δίεπ’: grammar allows only "rare verb διέπω"; note is hedged enough; kept "drove off".
- 24.268–274 harness: no allowed reference decides it; the notes already say tentative; only the ὀμφαλός error (change 17) was a real mistake. `l` kept literal.
- 24.209 "Portion"/"Fate": table (19.410) fixes this; kept.
- 24.228 κάλ’ ἐπιθήματα, 24.230: line 230 identical to Odyssey 24.276 and reused as shipped; 231 λευκά "white" is the Greek.
- 24.202 ἔκλε’ read as ἔκλεο: the only grammatical reading (imperfect middle of κλέω); kept.
- 24.201 ᾗς: taken as relative genitive; no better parse; kept.
- 24.214 `i` "that man": supplies Achilles for ἑ/κατέκτα; note says the Greek leaves him unnamed; kept.
- 24.239 note "away with you" as a gloss in a note, not a rendering: kept.
- 24.250 βοὴν ἀγαθός and 24.254 θοῇς: correct.
- 24.294 δεξιόν "a bird on the right": matches Odyssey 15.525 usage; kept.
- `μύθῳ` 200 `i` "answered him": the dative word is dropped from `i` only as a harmless fold; kept.

## Quotation marks

“ on 201, 218, 239, 253, 287, 300; ” on 215, 226, 244, 263, 296, 301; `mark` on the first unit of each speech (201, 218, 239, 253, 287, 300). Counts in `l` and `i` match. The opening unit 200 follows the closing ” of iliad-153's last unit.
